facts.raw_span: A 67-year-old man
hypertension, dyslipidaemia, stage 3 chronic kidney disease, active smoking (35 pack-years), a family history of ischaemic heart disease
prior percutaneous coronary interventions (2008, 2017, 2022) for non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction
Canadian Cardiovascular Society Class III angina
exercise stress test induced angina at 50 W without ECG changes
normal sinus rhythm, Q waves in lead III, and biphasic T waves in leads III and aVF
left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 65% without regional wall-motion abnormalities
patent stents in the circumflex artery, non-significant disease in the left anterior descending artery, and significant ostial right coronary artery stenosis
ST-segment elevation in leads V1–V3
subocclusion of the right coronary postero-lateral branch
recurrent sustained polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation
new QTc prolongation to 500 ms
A 67-year-old man
hypertension, dyslipidaemia, stage 3 chronic kidney disease, active smoking (35 pack-years), a family history of ischaemic heart disease
prior percutaneous coronary interventions (2008, 2017, 2022) for non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction
Canadian Cardiovascular Society Class III angina
exercise stress test induced angina at 50 W without ECG changes
normal sinus rhythm, Q waves in lead III, and biphasic T waves in leads III and aVF
left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 65% without regional wall-motion abnormalities
patent stents in the circumflex artery, non-significant disease in the left anterior descending artery, and significant ostial right coronary artery stenosis
ST-segment elevation in leads V1–V3
subocclusion of the right coronary postero-lateral branch
recurrent sustained polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation
new QTc prolongation to 500 ms

concepts.why: The patient has a history of non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction, prior percutaneous coronary interventions, and significant ostial right coronary artery stenosis, which are all consistent with acute coronary syndrome.

The patient developed ST-segment elevation, recurrent sustained polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, and ventricular fibrillation, followed by akinesia of all apical segments and severely reduced LVEF, which are all characteristic of takotsubo syndrome.

concepts.preferred_label: Myocardial Infarction with Non-Obstructive Coronary Arteries
concepts.why: The patient has a history of non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction, normal sinus rhythm, and ST-segment elevation, which could be consistent with myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries.

The patient has a history of hypertension, dyslipidaemia, stage 3 chronic kidney disease, active smoking, and prior percutaneous coronary interventions, which are all risk factors for coronary artery disease.
The patient developed recurrent sustained polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, which is a type of ventricular tachycardia.
The patient developed new QTc prolongation to 500 ms, which is consistent with long QT syndrome.
It explains the uncovered finding of subocclusion of the right coronary postero-lateral branch.

rationales.F02: The patient's history of hypertension, dyslipidaemia, and smoking suggests a high risk for coronary artery disease.
rationales.F03: Prior percutaneous coronary interventions suggest a history of coronary artery disease.
rationales.F08: The presence of significant ostial right coronary artery stenosis and patent stents in the circumflex artery suggests coronary artery disease.
rationales.F09: ST-segment elevation in leads V1–V3 is indicative of acute coronary syndrome.
rationales.F10: Subocclusion of the right coronary postero-lateral branch is consistent with coronary artery disease.
rationales.F11: Recurrent sustained polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation may be related to coronary artery disease or other cardiac conditions.
rationales.F12: New QTc prolongation to 500 ms is suggestive of long QT syndrome.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's presentation with ST-segment elevation, recurrent sustained polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, ventricular fibrillation, and new QTc prolongation, along with the development of akinesia of all apical segments and severely reduced LVEF, is highly suggestive of Takotsubo Syndrome, which is triggered by intense emotional or physical stress, consistent with the patient's anxious state and recent cardiac procedures.
